defect.statement: The typography observer ran the shared probe with no display scale. The probe host (Windows PowerShell 5.1) is DPI-unaware, so at a fractional display scale GetWindowRect/GetSystemMetrics stay in the DIP frame (1296x839 at (858,222)) while the display is physical (1620x1049 at (1072,278) at 125 %). The 7x7 display cross-check therefore compared two coordinate spaces and the capture was refused at 43 of 49 samples, below the required 45. The repair's measured effect (AX5: the same probe with the explicit 1.25 frame settles at 46/49) supports the mixed frame as the source of at least three of the six disagreements; 19.94's residual 'six disagreeing samples are not attributed' limitation still applies to the remaining three.

analysis_for_120_dpi.mapping: physical = round(dip * scale) with .NET Math.Round (half to even); the probe maps each display sample back into the DIP bitmap with round(px / scale) and clamps to the bitmap. At 1.25 the measured geometry is left 1072.5 -> 1072, top 277.5 -> 278, height 1048.75 -> 1049, matching the AX5 record.
analysis_for_120_dpi.why_43_49: with the legacy 1.0 frame the bitmap is still DIP-sized while the display samples are physical; 43 of the 49 sample pairs agree and 6 disagree, so the threshold (45) correctly refused the image.
analysis_for_120_dpi.why_46_49: with the 1.25 frame the display sample is mapped back into the DIP bitmap and 46 of 49 pairs agree (AX5 measured this deterministically: 4/4 raw runs and 3/3 observer runs with one PNG digest). Three pairs still disagree; their origin is not attributed here and does not affect the unchanged 45/49 gate.
analysis_for_120_dpi.repair_effect: the typography observer now receives that frame automatically from GetDpiForWindow(window)/96; the hermetic tests accept a 1.25 record with the measured geometry and refuse the legacy 1.0 record at the same scale.
analysis_for_120_dpi.not_measured_here: no new 120 DPI pixel result: the host is at 96 DPI and changing it is prohibited. The AX5 125 % numbers are cited as prior evidence from the same probe, not re-executed.
